assumptions.value: d = 137 pc, kappa(1.3 mm) ~3 cm2/g, T = 20 K

evidence.quote: Assuming a distance of 137 pc, a dust opacity at 1.3 mm of $\sim3\,$cm$^{2}$g$^{-1}$ (cite: andrews2011) and a temperature of 20 K

method.value: Fit real part of visibilities with three axisymmetric ring models (Gaussian, asymmetric Gaussian, Gaussian+power law), separately at each wavelength; PA and i from 1.3 mm fixed for 0.45 mm

evidence.quote: we obtained the PA and the $i$ using the 1.3 mm data (since it has better signal-to-noise) for each model, and keep the best-fit values of these two parameters to fit the 0.45 mm data.

key_parameters.value: radial grid 1-500 au in 0.1 au steps; 4000 steps, 1000 walkers, burn-in ~1000 steps

evidence.quote: for a total of 4000 steps with 1000 walkers.

fitting.value: emcee MCMC, Gaussian likelihood on real visibilities, uniform priors (e.g. Rpeak 1-100 au, Rwidth 1-50 au, i and PA 10-80 deg, x0,y0 +-0.2")

evidence.quote: We adopted a set of uniform prior probability distributions for the free parameters explored by the Markov chain in the three models

validation.value: Synthetic images and residuals made with identical uv coordinates; test with fixed uvmodelfit parameters; two-ring test

evidence.quote: We image the models and residuals (data-model) using identical $(u,v)$ coordinates as the actual ALMA observations.

results_numeric.quantity: Cavity depletion at 1.3 mm vs 0.45 mm

evidence.quote: the flux is reduced by around 85%

findings_qualitative.value: 13CO and C18O peak at the center of the mm cavity; neither dust nor gas detected in SR 24N

evidence.quote: we find that the $^{13}$CO and C$^{18}$O (J=2-1) emission peaks at the center of the continuum cavity.

claims.hypothesis: Does the ring narrow at longer wavelength as predicted by dust trapping?
claims.experiment: Visibility MCMC ring fits at 0.45 and 1.3 mm
claims.result: Ring peak ~20 au further out and ~10 au narrower at 1.3 mm
claims.finding: Consistent with pressure-bump trapping, though peak shift may be optical depth

evidence.quote: the peak of the ring is located further out and becomes narrower at longer wavelength

claims.hypothesis: Is gas present inside the mm cavity?
claims.experiment: 13CO and C18O moment maps and radial cuts
claims.finding: Gas not strongly depleted or cavity unresolved; low-mass planets or dead zone

evidence.quote: the gas emission is centrally peaking inside the mm-dust cavity

claims.hypothesis: Is SR 24N detected in dust or gas?
claims.result: ~3 sigma flux, no CO detection; dust mass <=0.12 Mearth
claims.finding: SR 24N poor in mm-grains and cold gas

evidence.quote: There is no detection of the dust continuum, $^{13}$CO, or C$^{18}$O emission at the location of the northern component (SR 24N)

claims.hypothesis: Is the ring emission optically thin?
claims.experiment: Brightness-temperature optical depth with literature temperatures
claims.result: tau>1 near the ring at both wavelengths
claims.finding: alpha_mm cannot be read as grain growth in the ring

evidence.quote: the emission is optically thick at both wavelengths ($\tau>1$) close to the location of the ring-like emission

why_this_method.value: Visibility modeling avoids deconvolution limits and can identify unresolved structures

evidence.quote: visibility modeling has some advantages over imaging analysis, since it can identify unresolved structures

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Internal photoevaporation ruled out as cavity origin

evidence.quote: this scenario can be ruled out as a potential origin for the mm-cavity in SR 24S

limitations_admitted.value: Gas masses not estimated due to foreground absorption

evidence.quote: because of the foreground absorption in some of the channels, we do not estimate gas masses from the current observations

limitations_admitted.value: Only real visibilities fit, so significance of asymmetry residuals unclear

evidence.quote: in the framework of our models, it is difficult to conclude how significant is the amount of residuals

referee_caveats_inferred: Optical thickness and assumed 20 K temperature make dust mass a rough lower estimate
Foreground cloud absorption contaminates CO lines; central peak may be affected
Fitting only real part with fixed PA/i for 0.45 mm; MCMC convergence settings loosely described
Different resolutions at the two wavelengths complicate the comparison of cavity depth
